title: How to pilot a product in vending machines
excerpt: Plan a vending product pilot with a pack-fit test, a refill owner, a stockout plan and a clear review decision.
opening: A product that sells well in a shop may present practical problems in a vending tray. A soft pack can catch, a bottle can tip and a label may be hard to read through glass. Run the pilot where you can check the pack, keep it stocked and learn what to change before adding sites.
checklist: Deliver actual retail packs for testing. Share dimensions, filled weight, storage conditions, shelf life and case quantity.
Agree on the slot type and verify repeated vends at different fill levels. Inspect the packs after each drop for damage.
Pick a small group of sites for a clear audience and buying occasion. Write down why each site was chosen.
Decide who owns stock, who refills it and who pays for waste, returns or unsold inventory. Agree on a minimum stock level and response time.
Check how the product appears in the machine and on the screen. Align its name, price and selection number so customers can find it.
Review units per in-stock machine-day, failed vends, stockouts, remaining shelf life and feedback. Agree what results justify expanding, adjusting the pack or stopping.
close: For example, a chilled tea pilot could use two workplaces and count how many days each machine actually had stock. Use that denominator when comparing the sites.
